summary: Investigated why the gizmo workspace's extension list omitted 'git': the supervised agent server's own log shows `spawn git ENOENT`, even though the server's PATH contains `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd`. Replayed that exact PATH in a normal Node process (git spawns fine) and ran the same probe under an S4U scheduled task (also fine, including absolute-path spawns), so the failure is not reproducible from these isolated tests. While probing, found and fixed a quoting typo in `pi-session-factory.ts` (`'\n'` instead of `'\n'`) and confirmed the supervisor relaunched the server cleanly.
decisions: Treated the git extension omission as a service-context issue rather than a PATH issue, because the same PATH string works in both a normal Node process and an S4U scheduled task probe — the exact failure mode in the live service could not be reproduced

Fixed a quoting bug in apps/agent-server/src/sessions/pi-session-factory.ts by changing ].join('\n'); to ].join('\n'); (escaped backslash before n), and verified tsc passes and the supervisor relaunched the server healthy on 8787/4173

Identified that Pi's commit-message generation uses completeSimple without attaching the x-opencode-session header that the 'Console Go' provider requires (returning MissingSessionID), with the header set in pi-coding-agent's provider-attribution.js
errors: Initial attempt to run Read-ProcEnv.ps1 failed because PowerShell resolved the relative path from the wrong cwd ('not recognized as a cmdlet...'); re-invoking with the absolute path succeeded
Remove-Item on the S4U probe output file was blocked by Windows protected-path policy; worked around by skipping the delete

A child_process spawn of `git` from inside the supervised agent-server process returns ENOENT even with Git\cmd on its Path; same spawn succeeds in a normal process and in a standalone S4U scheduled task probe, so the root cause remains unconfirmed
Pi's commit-message call returns 'MissingSessionID: Request is missing x-opencode-session' from the Console Go provider
